thread:
ivan: Heads-up — after yesterday's IdP cert + KMS key rotation one customer reported SCIM deprovisioning failing and some RBAC roles became orphaned. Getting 403 from our control plane when it calls the customer SCIM endpoint. logs attached below.
jess: Ugh. Is this the Private (VPC) customer or Hosted?
ivan: Private. They did IdP cert rotation and we rotated the signing key in KMS the same maintenance window.
alana: Can you paste the error trace? 403 from SCIM often means signature or auth header mismatch.
ivan: Pasted snippets:
```
2026-03-18T09:12:03.421Z controlplane-scim worker=12 trace_id=... DEBUG outgoing request to https://customer-scim.example.com/Users/abc123 - headers: Authorization: SAML sig=base64...
2026-03-18T09:12:03.422Z controlplane-scim worker=12 ERROR scim request failed status=403 body={"error":"invalid_signature","message":"signature verification failed"}
2026-03-18T09:12:03.423Z kms verifier service=keymgr warn=signature-verify-failed alg=RSASSA-PSS key=projects/prod/locations/global/keyRings/rw/keys/sso-sign-v2
```
jess: That alg=RSASSA-PSS in the KMS warn stands out. Some IdPs started offering PSS. Our SAML verifier only accepted RS1/RS256 previous to that patch.
mike: We ran a quick exploit triage — RBAC drift occurred because group->role deprovision webhook returned 403 and our retry/backoff left users in platform-admin for ~18 hours. We flagged as medium sev and started rollback.
alana: Any chance it's clock skew? signature verify can fail if timestamps off.
ivan: We checked NTP — clocks within 3s. Also saw the customer's SAML assertion `SignatureMethod Algorithm` header: `http://www.w3.org/2007/05/xmldsig-more#rsa-pss` which maps to PSS.
jess: Ok that explains it. PSS isn't wire-compatible with our verifier. Two quick remediation options: 1) fallback to previous KMS key that used RS256 (if they still have previous cert) OR 2) add PSS verification to our runtime.
security-bot: :warning: Note: PSS vs RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 differences could affect verification library. Confirm dependencies before enabling.
mike: For immediate mitigation we toggled the control-plane SCIM client to use 'saml-signed-fallback=true' which makes control plane accept unsigned Authorization if the request comes from the customer's VPC (trusted network). Risky but limited to one customer for 2h while we patch.
alana: Can you paste the SAML signature headers we saw?
ivan: From the customer's assertion: `SignatureMethod Algorithm="http://www.w3.org/2007/05/xmldsig-more#rsa-pss"` and in the raw log: `SignatureValue: MIIB...`
jess: Also check the KMS key metadata: we rotated to a key with `purpose=ASYMMETRIC_SIGN` and `algorithm=RSA_SIGN_PSS_2048_SHA256`. Our verifier was only configured for `RSA_SIGN_PKCS1_2048_SHA256`.
ivan: Ran `gcloud kms keys versions get-public-key` and confirmed.
```
$ gcloud kms keys versions get-public-key 1 --location=global --keyring=rw --key=sso-sign-v2 --format='get(pem)' > pub.pem
$ openssl rsa -pubin -in pub.pem -text -noout
Public-Key: (2048 bit)
Modulus: ...
```
```
controlplane error: verify: unsupported padding scheme: rsa-pss
```
jess: Good repro. Plan: patch verifier to accept PSS (with explicit salt length = hash size) and add test harness that fetches public key from KMS and verifies a signed assertion. Also add pre-rotation check to our KMS rotation runbook: when you create new key, ensure consumers (control-plane verifiers) support the alg.
mike: For the RBAC audit gap: we generated a one-off remediation job to remove `platform-admin` from users who lost SCIM group membership. Patch applied at 09:50 UTC. Also raised a vuln-triage ticket because the fallback left a short window of elevated privileges.
alana: Can we avoid the fallback in the future? maybe staged rollouts for key rotations: create new key, allow both algs for N days, then deprecate.
jess: Agreed. Also add a unit test in eng-runtime that exercises both PKCS#1 v1.5 and PSS verification modes.
security-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026-453 (postmortem + runbook update) and linked incident playbook.
ivan: Customer updated IdP metadata to use RSASSA-PKCS1 (they could) but they prefer PSS. We decided to support PSS — patched runtime and rolled to canary cluster at 11:20. Canary verified SCIM calls succeed and deprovisions resumed.
mike: Post-deploy verification: curl to their SCIM endpoint via control plane returned 204 for DELETE and 200 for GET.
```
curl -i -X DELETE https://customer-scim.example.com/Users/abc123 -H "Authorization: SAML sig=..."
HTTP/1.1 204 No Content
```
jess: Follow-ups: 1) Add KMS key-rotation preflight check that validates alg compatibility and fails the rotation if incompatible, 2) Add e2e SCIM regression tests that run after rotation in staging, 3) Update RBAC audit to have a 'auto-remediate' job that undoes orphaned roles within 30 minutes.
alana: Also add a compliance note — rotation windows must notify Security 48h in advance for Private customers.
ivan: I'm drafting the postmortem now — will include timelines, mitigation steps, and the PR that added PSS support.
mike: Thx — looks like root cause: KMS key rotation + alg mismatch (RSA-PSS vs PKCS1) + immediate removal of fallback + missing pre-rotation validation.
jess: Closing the immediate thread: mark as resolved once postmortem available and runbook updated. :white_check_mark:
ivan: Thanks team. Learned a lot about padding schemes today. :grimacing:
security-bot: Incident closed, link to SEC-2026-453: https://redwood.company/security/SEC-2026-453
